spec_match.rationale: The demos exercise the exact contract: the computed value of each overflow pair, and whether the resulting axis is a scrollport. Scrollability is measured by assigning a scroll offset and reading it back rather than inferred from the computed keyword, which is what makes the clip-to-hidden coercion visible instead of merely stated.

interactive.rationale: A 25-pair matrix with a highlighted, keyboard-scrollable live sample; three strips whose buried control can be focused to trigger the browser's own scroll-into-view; and a sheet whose scroll offset is driven by a slider with the sticky header's position measured against a reference lane.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index leads with the practical consequence — hidden is still a scrollport, so the axis you switched off can still be scrolled — which is the CSSWG change's own motivation, and each card matches its page.

edge_cases.rationale: All 25 pairs including the symmetric visible coercion, shorthand versus longhand spellings measured separately, the sheet scrolled past the end of the grid, and a reset path for each demo.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5067363861004288 on the index and all three concept pages, with CSSWG PR 13903, CSS Overflow 3 and CSS Positioned Layout 3.

conformance.rationale: Seven immutable assertions: two-value syntax, clip-alone not scrolling, hidden genuinely scrolling, the visible→auto coercion as the symmetric reference, clip surviving beside a scrollable value, the consequence (inline axis scrolls, block axis refuses), and shorthand/longhand agreement.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150, twice. Flag off (3/3, 21 assertions): every mismatched pair coerces clip to hidden, all three strips scroll 128px on an axis with no scrollbar, and the sticky header drifts 160px. Flag on, --enable-experimental-web-platform-features (3/3, 21 assertions): scroll clip computes to scroll/clip, nine pairs keep their clip, only the hidden lane scrolls on focus, and both sticky headers pin at 0px. The pages report whichever world they are in without editing.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the measured coercion counts, which lanes moved, and the measured sticky offsets.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px minimums on controls including the range input, and the 25-row matrix scrolls inside its own container rather than widening the page.

accessibility.rationale: The live sample is a focusable region with an accessible name so the axis behaviour can be felt from the keyboard; lanes are articles labelled by their headings; every verdict is text as well as a border colour; results are announced through aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Lane and strip grids are auto-fit minmax with align-content:start; the pair matrix is inside overflow-x:auto because 25 rows of six nowrap columns cannot fit 360px and should not try.

openQuestions.title: Re-measure once the clip pairing ships, and let the pages say so on their own
openQuestions.detail: Every page already branches on what it measures, so no code changes when Chrome 153 lands: the matrix will show clip surviving, the strips will stop scrolling on focus, and the sticky lane will pin. What is worth revisiting is the copy that currently explains the coercion in the present tense — it should read as well after the change as before, and the conditional branches were written for that, but they have only ever been exercised on the pre-153 side.

openQuestions.title: Add a touch-gesture angle
openQuestions.detail: The focus-driven scroll is one route into an accidental scrollport; a touch drag that starts inside the strip is another, and it behaves differently again because the compositor decides which axis takes the gesture. That deserves its own page rather than being folded into the focus demo, and it needs a real touch device to build honestly.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use auto-fit grids with intrinsic minimums for panels; give inherently wide content its own scroll container rather than letting the page scroll sideways.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Lane grids use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280–300px, 1fr)) with align-content:start; the 25-row pair matrix is wrapped in .scroller (overflow-x:auto) because its columns are nowrap by design — the values being compared must not wrap.

guidanceConsulted.query: live region for results updated by a button
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce measured state changes in text, and never encode a result in colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Every lane's verdict is a sentence naming the measured pixel value; border colour is redundant with it. Each page writes an aria-live summary on every recompute.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive asserts the verdict text and the detail text on each lane.

guidanceConsulted.query: overflow clip versus hidden clipping boundary
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer overflow:clip where an axis genuinely should not scroll, and be aware that clip and hidden differ in whether a scrollport is created.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: This is the feature under demonstration, so the guidance is the subject rather than an implementation choice; the pages measure the difference instead of asserting it, and the accidental-scrollport page exists precisely because the distinction is invisible until something scrolls.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Measured: overflow:hidden takes a 50px offset, overflow:clip refuses it — both asserted in the conformance suite.

summary: Three concepts built around one measurable fact: hidden is a scroll container and clip is not, so an axis coerced from clip to hidden is still scrollable by focus, by script, and by the browser itself. On this pre-153 build every mismatched pair coerces, and all three demos report that plainly rather than pretending otherwise.
